title: LLMs Assist NLP Researchers: Critique Paper (Meta-)Reviewing

paper.authors: Du, Wang, Zhao, Deng, Liu, Lou, Zou, Venkit, Zhang, Srinath, et al. (arXiv 2406.16253)
paper.repo_license: Apache NON-AI License 2.0 (research only; no use for model training)
paper.repo_commit: 629932bcfa31879b1df1e011e3cd7188aa3b9b46 (clone external/repos/W4404782918/jiangshdd__ReviewCritique; dataset only, no code). github.com/Tiiiger/bert_score is a third-party metric tool, not the paper's repo.

dependence.note: Thread (ii) 'LLMs as Metareviewers': the LLM is evaluated on flagging expert-labelled Deficient review segments; the numbers are the model's own precision/recall/F1 against human expert annotations. (Thread (i) 'LLMs as Reviewers' uses LLM-generated reviews judged by humans and is not automatable.)

claim.statement: LLMs are poor meta-reviewers: prompted to flag Deficient review segments on ReviewCritique, GPT-4 (API alias gpt-4-turbo) reaches only precision / recall / F1 = 17.18 / 34.59 / 20.30 with the Select-Deficient prompt and 14.91 / 34.49 / 18.38 with Labeling-All (ensembles 16.85 / 20.66); recall exceeds precision for every model, and the best F1 across all models is 21.99 (Claude Opus, Either-No ensemble) (Table 4). Explanations for correctly flagged segments score ROUGE-1/2/L 17.13 / 2.71 / 14.64 and BERTScore 55.63 for GPT-4 (Table 5).
claim.metric: Segment-level precision, recall and F1 for the Deficient class (reliability == 'No'), computed per paper then averaged across papers (Sec. 4.2); explanation quality via ROUGE and BERTScore (microsoft/deberta-xlarge-mnli) on correctly identified segments
claim.original_source: Paper Table 4 and Table 5 (Sec. 4.2), Table 1 (dataset stats), Tables 10-11 (appendix E, all prompt conditions), Appendix A.3 (model endpoints)

protocol.model: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09. Paper (Appendix A.3): 'GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo)' - an undated alias. Experiments ran between the 2024-04-09 GA release (when the alias started resolving to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) and the arXiv v1 date 2024-06-24, so the alias can only have resolved to 2024-04-09. The paper genuinely USED this model as an experimental arm.
protocol.prompt_source: appendix F: Table 12 (Labeling-All) and Table 13 (Select-Deficient), verbatim in the paper; not in repo. Placeholders {paper_title}, {body_text}, {review_text} (indexed segments), {author_rebuttals_text}

messages.content: Assume you are a meta-reviewer of a natural language processing conference. Given a paper submission and its corresponding review, your job is to assess the deficiency of each review segment. ... The criteria for Deficient are: 1. factual errors or misinterpretations ... 2. lacking constructive feedback 3. overly subjective, emotional, or offensive judgments ... 4. downsides without supporting evidence ... Here is the submission title: {paper_title} Here is the body text of the submission: {body_text} Here is the segmented review: {review_text} Here is the author rebuttals: {author_rebuttals_text} ... [index]. [Yes or No][Your explanation if your answer is No] Output your answer below:

protocol.n_items: 380 human-written reviews over 100 ICLR submissions (50 accepted / 50 rejected), 11,376 segments; one call per review per prompt strategy (assumed: Table 4 caption says 'on our ReviewCritique dataset'; the exact subset is not restated)
protocol.samples_per_item: 1 per prompt strategy x 2 strategies (Labeling-All, Select-Deficient); ensembles derived offline
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: parse '[index]. [Yes/No] explanation' lines, align to segment indices, compare with reliability labels (Yes = reliable, No = Deficient), P/R/F1 per paper then mean; ROUGE + BERTScore (deberta-xlarge-mnli) between model explanation and expert explanation for true positives. No code released; parsing/alignment rules must be written by us.
protocol.environment_check: Load data/ReviewCritique.jsonl (100 records; keys decision, title, body_text, review#1..#4 -> review[{segment_text, topic_class_1, topic_class_2, reliability, explanation, error_type}], score) and confirm 380 reviews / 11,376 segments / 712 'No' labels (paper says 713); measure prompt lengths (body_text mean ~41.6k chars ~ 10.4k tokens, max ~155k chars ~ 39k tokens - all within 128k).

artifacts.data_path: data/ReviewCritique.jsonl (100 papers, human reviews with segment labels); data/ReviewCritique_LLM.jsonl (20 papers, LLM-generated reviews by gpt4 / claude_opus / gemini_pro_1.5 with labels; thread (i))
artifacts.data_license: Apache NON-AI License 2.0 - evaluation/analysis/benchmarking allowed, training forbidden; derivative works must state origin. Paper bodies are ICLR OpenReview submissions (initial versions).
artifacts.notes: The prompt has an {author_rebuttals_text} slot but the released JSONL has no rebuttal field; rebuttals would have to be scraped from OpenReview (all 100 are public ICLR submissions) or the slot left empty (documented deviation). Segment count 712 vs 713 minor mismatch.

blockers: author rebuttal texts used in the prompt are absent from the released data (fetch from OpenReview or run without - deviation)
decoding parameters (temperature, max_tokens) and output-parsing / index-alignment rules unreported; no evaluation code
exact evaluation subset for Table 4 not restated (assumed all 380 human reviews)
long-context prompts (mean ~12.5k tokens incl. review; max ~40k) - cost-dominant and sensitive to any truncation policy
BERTScore/ROUGE secondary metric needs the deberta-xlarge-mnli checkpoint (public)

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (paper's GPT-4 = alias gpt-4-turbo, mid-2024)

successors: claude (current Sonnet/Opus id per target_models; paper's claude-3-opus-20240229 is dead)
gemini (current Pro/Flash id; paper's gemini-1.5-flash is dead)
llama (open weights, pinned hash; paper used Llama-3-8B/70B-Instruct with 8k truncation)
qwen (open weights, pinned hash; paper lists Qwen2-72B but endpoint string says Qwen2-7B-Instruct)

budget.sampling_scheme: temperature 0 (unreported -> ANALYSIS_PLAN default) x 3 seeds; 2 prompt strategies are the paper's own paraphrase pair

full.note: 380 reviews x 2 prompts = 760 calls/seed x 3 seeds; ~12.5k input tokens (paper body mean 10.4k + segmented review ~1.5k + instructions) and ~700 output tokens (Labeling-All lists every segment); ~111 USD/seed; no prompt-caching discount assumed

representative_subset.note: the 20-paper subset (60 human reviews, Table 1 col 4) x 2 prompts x 3 seeds = 360 calls; ~18 USD/seed; preserves per-paper F1 averaging and both prompt strategies

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1 on Select-Deficient F1 (primary; 20.30) with Labeling-All F1 (18.38) as secondary: survival = re-run mean F1 within the bootstrap 95% CI over papers of the original AND recall > precision AND F1 stays in the 'relatively low' regime (< ~30). Partial = direction (recall > precision, low F1) holds but F1 leaves the CI. Dead = F1 rises to a level contradicting 'LLMs struggle' (e.g. > 35) or precision/recall ordering reverses.
judgment.notes: Per-paper F1 with ~4 reviews and ~7 Deficient segments per paper is noisy; report bootstrap CI over 100 papers (or 20 for the subset).

status_reason: live arm gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 genuinely used (alias gpt-4-turbo, mid-2024); data public; prompts verbatim in appendix; remaining gaps are protocol details (rebuttals, decoding, parsing)
user_checks: Accept Select-Deficient F1 = 20.30 (Table 4) as the single judged number, with Labeling-All as secondary?
Rebuttal slot: scrape author rebuttals from OpenReview for the 100 ICLR submissions, or run with the slot empty and record the deviation?
Run all 380 reviews (~335 USD for 3 seeds) or the 20-paper / 60-review subset (~53 USD)?
Temperature 0 and max_tokens 4096 as defaults (both unreported)?
Parsing rule for unparseable or missing indices: treat as 'Yes' (reliable)? Authors did not specify
domain_notes: Capability-limit claim about LLMs judging peer reviews; humans (senior NLP researchers) provide the gold labels, so the metric is fully automatic once labels exist. The prompt carries the entire paper body (mean ~10k tokens), so this card is token-heavy per call and should use the dated snapshot explicitly (the paper only gives the alias). The dataset licence forbids training use and asks for attribution; our L1 log archive will contain the paper texts (public OpenReview submissions), which is permitted for evaluation/analysis.
